text: Socrates argues that identifying knowledge with perception, once wedded to Protagoras' claim that 'man is the measure of all things,' collapses into a self-refuting relativism: if every belief is true for whoever holds it, then the belief that Protagoras' doctrine is false is likewise true for those who hold it.
explanation: This is precisely the self-refutation argument in the Theaetetus: Protagorean relativism, which knowledge-as-perception entails, must grant the truth (for them) of its own critics' rejection of it, and so undermines itself. It is among the earliest self-refutation arguments deployed against global relativism.
